requirements.why: The handshake is how the INS address book knows which notification and role to return the new address to; it stays because the INS frontend remains the address book's only writer (c-106). DR1 asked for a route to add an address from every address-selection page (inc-053), and it now exists.
requirements.deltaNote: Built today: the picker offers 'Add a new address' beside its heading and sends the four parameters to the INS add page (repo-frontend-p15-056, repo-frontend-p15-057), the contact page offers its own 'add a new branch address' link (repo-tests-p7-013), all five pickers are proven to open the page (repo-tests-p7-002), the handshake comes back unchanged (trace-e2e-p9-070-m1) and stub mode offers neither the add control nor the View links (repo-frontend-p15-036).

requirements.statement: The journey's address-return route accepts a return only when its fulfilment id names a role and its handshake token matches the single-use token the picker issued for that role, a missing, reused or mismatched token included, and looks the returned address id up in the signed-in organisation's own address book.
requirements.why: Stops a forged or replayed return from writing another organisation's address, or any address, into a notification.
requirements.deltaNote: The return route is built and carries the fulfilment id and token back unchanged, with a fresh token on every render of the picker (trace-e2e-p9-016, trace-e2e-p9-070, trace-e2e-p9-070-m1); what no source in this area shows is a missing, expired, reused or mismatched token being refused (trace-e2e-p9-078), so the refusals are what is left to prove.

requirements.statement: When a return cannot be completed, the trader goes back to the role's picker: an address that is not found or is deleted shows 'The address could not be found in your address book. requirements.why: A failed return must leave the trader somewhere they can carry on, with a reason they can act on.
requirements.deltaNote: Built today: the picker opens with the not-found message (repo-frontend-p15-059) or the unreachable message, marked as a recoverable error (repo-frontend-p15-060).

requirements.deltaNote: The link is on the page and lands on the Overview saving nothing, leaving the role with only its add link (repo-tests-p7-003, repo-tests-p7-009, repo-tests-p7-010); the traces still show a 'Cancel and return to address page' button (trace-e2e-p9-075, c-party-address-add-and-edit-002).

requirements.statement: An address added from the journey is saved into the signed-in organisation's address book with its email and phone, and is then listed in the address book and in every role picker.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree that a journey-added address joins the shared book.
requirements.deltaNote: A newly added address is listed in the picker and above the branch addresses already in the book (repo-tests-p7-008, repo-tests-p7-018), created through the organisation-scoped address book API (trace-e2e-p8-011).

requirements.statement: The add-address page is built from GOV.UK Frontend components (input, select, checkboxes, hint, error summary, notification banner, buttons, back link, width classes); the address search is the one component outside the toolbox, because GOV.UK Frontend has none.
requirements.why: The prototype's app-* field and heading classes are its own implementation, not a difference a trader sees.
requirements.deltaNote: The page uses only GOV.UK Frontend components (trace-e2e-p9-068).

requirements.statement: The add-address round trip (both saves and cancel) is proven end to end from every role picker and from the consignment contact page.
requirements.why: Each picker issues its own fulfilment id, so a return that works from one proves nothing about the rest.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the add control is proven to open the page from all five pickers (repo-tests-p7-002), but each of the two saves and the cancel is proven once only (repo-tests-p7-004, repo-tests-p7-007, repo-tests-p7-009), the traces drove the round trip from the consignor picker alone (trace-e2e-p9-077), and the hand-off is skipped in stub mode so no fit spec covers it (repo-tests-p7-001, repo-frontend-p15-146).

requirements.statement: A picked or added address is copied onto the notification, not linked: renaming, moving or deleting the address book record later leaves the draft's copy as it was, with no error, and the picker then neither preselects nor offers a deleted record.
requirements.why: A notification must hold the address it was made with; Design Release 2.1 also stores a copy on the section.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven today: a chosen address is copied rather than referenced (repo-frontend-p15-063), a deleted or role-less record counts as no selection (repo-frontend-p15-055), and the copy survives renaming and deletion of the record (trace-e2e-p8-001, trace-e2e-p8-006, repo-tests-p7-061).

requirements.statement: On the review page each consignment party and the contact address read back as the name followed by the address lines and country (GB shown as 'United Kingdom'), each on its own line, without the telephone number or email address, under a card titled 'Consignment addresses'. The plants frontend's check-answers place of destination, consignor and contact cards read back the same way, in the same increment: the name, then one line per address line, then the country, with no telephone number and no email address row.
requirements.why: The trader checks the copy the notification holds before submitting, and the owner's 17 November decision gives the addresses the same wording on check your answers, the overview task list and the addresses page. Plants has the same party cards, so it takes the same change at the same time (ruling 2026-10-09 pm), which withdraws plants' own d-013 addition of telephone and email to the contact card (c-293). The address-book record still carries both.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the review shows each copied address as a block, name in bold then each non-empty field on its own line, telephone and email included (trace-e2e-p8-004, trace-e2e-p8-018), and the review already carries a 'Consignment addresses' card and a separate 'Contact address' card (repo-tests-p7-067, repo-tests-p7-068). Plants' party cards today carry Name, Address, Telephone number and Email address rows with the address joined by commas, and lose telephone and email and read line by line in the same increment (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-045); the plants repo claims that show today's cards sit in the party-cards area's working set, not this one. The overview-and-review area writes the same card title, so the cross-area pass merges the two.

requirements.statement: Each role and the consignment contact has its own page for editing the copy the notification holds, at the role's own edit path, reached from the hub's and review page's 'Edit details' links; in the high-risk plants frontend the same page serves each party plants holds.
requirements.why: The address book accepts records that break the notification's address rules, so a notification needs a way to correct its own copy without touching the book: a real validation and cross-service constraint the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven today in both frontends: six edit pages in live animals (repo-frontend-p15-096, repo-frontend-p15-003) and three in plants (repo-plantsfrontend-p8-052), reached from the 'Edit details' link (repo-tests-p7-055, repo-tests-p7-056). Design Release 2.1 shows no such page; it is kept because rule-breaking copies need it (req-694).

requirements.statement: The party edit page is headed 'Edit address details', captioned with the party's own title ('Place of origin', 'Consignor', 'Consignee', 'Importer', 'Place of destination' or 'Contact address for consignment'), titled 'Edit address details - Import notification service - GOV.UK', below the notification's journey strip.
requirements.why: The merged consignor-and-exporter party is the single Consignor, as the design's own section heading reads and the service's role vocabulary already holds, so the caption names the party once.
requirements.deltaNote: The heading, the title and the strip are built (repo-frontend-p15-098, repo-frontend-p15-098-m1, trace-e2e-p8-032-m1, trace-e2e-p8-090), and the consignor's caption reads 'Consignor or exporter' today, which names a party the service does not model and no role vocabulary holds (ruling-ian-2026-11-16-p1-029, ruling-ian-2026-11-16-p1-035). Plants already captions the same page with the party's own title (repo-plantsfrontend-p8-053), so plants needs no change here.

requirements.statement: The party edit page explains 'Changes apply to this notification only. Your address book is not changed.'
requirements.why: The trader must know the edit does not reach the book.
requirements.deltaNote: Built in both frontends (repo-frontend-p15-099, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-054, repo-tests-p7-057).

requirements.statement: The party edit page asks for 'Name or organisation name', 'Address line 1', 'Address line 2 (optional)', 'Town or city', 'County (optional)', 'Postcode or Zip code' (width 10), 'Country' (a plain select, 'Select a country' then the address book's country list), 'Phone number' (hint 'For international numbers include the country code') and 'Email address', in that order; only address line 2 and county are optional.
requirements.why: The page sets every field the address book record carries, so a corrected copy loses nothing. Its Country stays a plain select in this programme: the animals party address country's autocomplete is a follow-on ticket recorded in deferred.md (ruling 2026-10-09 pm).
requirements.deltaNote: Built today with these nine fields in this order in both frontends (repo-frontend-p15-100, repo-frontend-p15-101, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-056, repo-tests-p7-059, trace-e2e-p8-035 to trace-e2e-p8-044).

requirements.statement: The party edit page's buttons are 'Save changes' and a secondary 'Cancel', with no save-and-return-to-overview control.
requirements.why: The page is an aside from a picker or from the review, not a step of the journey.
requirements.deltaNote: Built in both frontends (repo-frontend-p15-120, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-070, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-072, trace-e2e-p8-045).

requirements.statement: The party edit page opens pre-filled with every field of the notification's copy, the country select set to its code; before any address is picked for that party it sends the trader to the party's picker and saves nothing.
requirements.why: There is nothing to edit until a copy exists.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven in both frontends (repo-frontend-p15-121, repo-frontend-p15-131, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-078, repo-tests-p7-058, trace-e2e-p8-034).

requirements.statement: The party edit page applies the address book's rules and messages: 'Enter a name', 'Enter address line 1', 'Enter a town or city', 'Enter a postcode', 'Enter a country' for a blank country, 'Enter a telephone number', 'Enter an email address', plus the length caps and the email-format check, with address line 2 and county never required.
requirements.why: The copy must meet the same rules the address book sets, so a corrected copy is valid.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven today (repo-frontend-p15-110 to repo-frontend-p15-119, repo-tests-p7-063, trace-e2e-p8-048, trace-e2e-p8-051), and plants copies the same rules and sentences from the address book (repo-plantsfrontend-p8-092, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-093).

requirements.statement: A refused edit answers 400, re-renders 'Edit address details' with the error summary and an error on each field, keeps what was typed (the country select resets to 'Select a country' for an unlisted value) and saves nothing; browser validation is off.
requirements.why: A refused edit must leave the notification's copy as it was, and the owner's 26 October decision is that a save with a missing or invalid answer keeps the trader on the page with an error for each one and what they entered kept.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven in both frontends (repo-frontend-p15-130, repo-frontend-p15-133, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-084-m1, repo-tests-p7-064, trace-e2e-p8-047, trace-e2e-p8-053).

requirements.statement: A valid edit replaces only this notification's copy of the party: the address book record and any other notification holding a copy of it are unchanged, the party's picker opens with no address preselected, and no banner is shown.
requirements.why: The copy belongs to the notification.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven in both frontends (repo-frontend-p15-122 to repo-frontend-p15-124, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-082, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-083, repo-tests-p7-061, repo-tests-p7-062, repo-tests-p7-071, trace-e2e-p8-028).

requirements.statement: Save, Cancel and Back on the party edit page return to where the edit was started, named by its return marker from a closed list (the addresses hub, the review page or the contact picker in live animals; check-your-answers or one of the three pickers in plants), falling back to the party's own picker and keeping the trail; Cancel discards what was typed.
requirements.why: The trader comes back to the page they left.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven in both frontends (repo-frontend-p15-126, repo-frontend-p15-127, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-088, repo-tests-p7-065, repo-tests-p7-066, trace-e2e-p8-057, trace-e2e-p8-058).

requirements.statement: If saving an edit fails with a recoverable backend error, the party edit page re-renders with status 500 and the recoverable-error message, and the held copy is unchanged.
requirements.why: A failed save must not lose or corrupt the copy.
requirements.deltaNote: Built in both frontends (repo-frontend-p15-132, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-090).

requirements.statement: The party edit page has Welsh copy for every piece of wording it shows, the character-limit sentences included, marked as a machine draft not yet reviewed by a translator.
requirements.why: Today's Welsh copy, which needs Welsh Language Standards sign-off before it ships to users.
requirements.deltaNote: Present in both frontends and marked as a machine draft (repo-frontend-p15-142, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-127, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-128).

requirements.statement: The party edit page is built only from GOV.UK Frontend components and has no serious or critical accessibility violations against WCAG 2.2 AA.
requirements.why: Accessibility.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven in both frontends (repo-frontend-p15-140, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-124, trace-animals-fit-p15-067).

requirements.statement: A copy is checked against the notification's address rules: the address book accepts a record the rules refuse (such as a country name rather than a listed code), the picker lets the trader pick it, and its edit form then opens with no country selected.
requirements.why: The address book only checks a country is present, so the notification must catch a copy that breaks its rules.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven today (repo-frontend-p15-109, repo-tests-p7-063-m1, trace-e2e-p8-013, trace-e2e-p8-022), and plants can check a held copy the same way (repo-plantsfrontend-p8-126).

requirements.statement: On the review page an answered party whose copied address breaks the address-book rules is named in a 'There is a problem' error summary ('Correct the address details for the <role>', 'Correct the contact address details for this consignment'), linked to that party's edit page with return=notification-view and repeated inside the party's row; a stored answer that has become invalid is named on its card; these entries come before the unfinished-card entries, and either stops Continue.
requirements.why: The trader must see which copy to correct and get straight to it. The single-app prototype holds no copy that can break a rule, so it cannot express these errors (c-139).
requirements.deltaNote: Proven today end to end (trace-e2e-p8-015, trace-e2e-p8-016, trace-e2e-p8-017, trace-e2e-p8-019), and plants links its own check-answers refusal straight to the party's edit page (repo-plantsfrontend-p8-118).

requirements.statement: While a copy breaks the rules, Continue on the review page is refused (400, same error summary) and a direct declaration submit is refused and sent back to the review page.
requirements.why: A notification with an invalid party address must not be submitted, and the review page is where submission is refused.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven today (trace-e2e-p8-020, trace-e2e-p8-020-m1, trace-e2e-p8-021).

requirements.statement: Correcting the copy on its edit page and saving returns to the review page with the error gone, after which the trader can continue to the Declaration and submit to 'Import notification submitted'.
requirements.why: Correction must unblock submission.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven today (trace-e2e-p8-023, trace-e2e-p8-024).

requirements.statement: Once a notification is submitted its copied addresses are frozen: renaming, moving or deleting the address book record changes neither the submitted view, whose status tag reads 'Submitted' and which offers no Change or Edit details links, nor an amendment, neither shows an error, and cancelling the amendment restores the submitted copy.
requirements.why: A submitted notification is a record of what was declared, and a notification submitted with outstanding items is SUBMITTED like any other, no separate status being introduced.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven today (trace-e2e-p8-081, trace-e2e-p8-084, trace-e2e-p8-085), with one gap: no source edits a copy during an amendment and then cancels it (trace-e2e-p8-097).

requirements.statement: Until address search is built, every add-address page reached from the journey opens with the address and contact fields and the roles checkboxes shown at once, with no search box and no 'Enter address manually' control, so a trader can add any party's address by hand.
requirements.why: Ruling 2026-10-09 blocks address search on the address lookup becoming a real feature and ruling 2026-11-09 parks it as concept work, while manual address entry is built now; a destination-side page that hid its fields behind a search that does not exist would leave no way to add the address.
requirements.deltaNote: The page shows its nine fields and, from a party picker, the roles checkboxes at once for every role, with no search (repo-tests-p7-015, repo-tests-p7-027, repo-tests-p7-031), which is what the owner's 9 November decision keeps (ruling-sam-2026-11-09-p1-014).

requirements.statement: A trader adding an address from a germinal products notification's party picker crosses to the INS address book by the same handshake and the same add page, with the same address record and rules as live animals. The INS address book accepts the germinal products set as well as live animals, and saving or cancelling returns to the germinal set's own address-return page under /germinal-products/notifications/{notification id}, built on the server from a registered entry in the INS service's conventions, never to a live-animals notification.
requirements.why: Germinal products is a sibling set with its own journey, routes and cookies that takes live animals as its reference point for everything, and its notifications keep GBN-AG references; ruling 2026-10-09 puts the address-book return entry for the germinal set in the INS themes, proven in the ins Playwright project.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the handshake carries journey-type 'gbn-ag' and the INS address book returns to the live-animals journey's address-return route (trace-e2e-p9-014, trace-e2e-p9-070, repo-frontend-p15-057); no germinal set exists yet.

requirements.statement: With JavaScript, address search results appear as the trader types, with the typed text in bold in each result.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's type-ahead on the address lookup. Design's 13 November decision settles only that the picker's address search does not filter as the trader types and expressly leaves the lookup's results-as-you-type to the deferred concept work, so this waits on design question 10 and on the lookup; the search works without it by its Search button (req-648).
requirements.deltaNote: No address search exists today (repo-frontend-p15-149, trace-e2e-p9-058).
requirements.blockedBy: Parked by ruling:sam-2026-11-09 points 2 and 3: address search is concept work, not needed for the deadline, and ruling:design-2026-11-13 point 4 leaves the lookup's results-as-you-type with that concept work rather than settling it. When it is planned, design answers design question 10 (address search layout) in the waiting-on-design theme; it is also blocked until the INS backend's address lookup becomes a real feature, after which the address search area is re-distilled.

requirements.statement: When the add page is reached from the journey, it skips the address book's 'Choose an address type' step and opens the 'Add address and contact details' step for the type the party implies, with that party's role already held as one of the address's roles.
requirements.why: The section the trader came from already says what kind of address it is (DR1 inc-053, c-106's outcome); asking again would be a wasted step, and the address type is the front door's grouping of roles rather than anything stored, so the role the page was reached for settles it.
requirements.deltaNote: Today there is no type step at all: the journey lands straight on the address and contact fields (trace-e2e-p9-055, repo-tests-p7-027, repo-tests-p7-014). The skip is new logic that must ship with the address book's type step (address-book-add-and-edit).

requirements.statement: A picker search that matches nothing ('No addresses match your search.') still shows the 'Add a new address' control above the picker form, so a trader whose address is not in the book can add it from there.
requirements.why: DR1 found the empty search a dead end (inc-053); the add control now sits beside the picker's heading whatever the search finds.
requirements.deltaNote: The picker renders the add control beside its heading whenever the service is not in stub mode, independent of the search results, and shows 'No addresses match your search.' in place of the count (repo-frontend-p15-056, repo-frontend-p15-036, repo-frontend-p15-023). The empty-state wording itself is the party picker area's.

requirements.statement: Each picker row offers a link to that saved address's own record in the INS address book, carrying the picker in a return parameter so the trader can correct or delete the book record and come back to the picker they left, under a column headed by the visually hidden word 'Actions'.
requirements.why: DR1 asked for a way to correct a wrong saved address from the picker (inc-054), built together with the add route and leading to the same place; the INS frontend is the address book's only writer (c-106), so the record and its edit live there.
requirements.deltaNote: Built today: each row offers a 'View' link named for the address, going to the INS address book's own page for the record with a return query naming the picker, its search term and its page number, under an 'Actions' column shown only outside stub mode (repo-frontend-p15-034, repo-frontend-p15-035, repo-frontend-p15-026, repo-frontend-p15-036). The in-place 'View details' disclosure DR1 found has gone with it (document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-036). Animals only: plants is not wired to the INS address book (ruling 2026-10-09 pm). What is left is the proof, because the fit suite runs in stub mode where the link is not offered (repo-frontend-p15-146).

requirements.statement: Out of scope here: transporter list rows linking to a saved transporter's own record page.
requirements.why: A transporter is its own record in its own transporters collection inside the address book service rather than an Address, and it holds no role, so the link DR1 asked for on the transporter list belongs to the transporter work and not to this area's address pickers.

requirements.statement: Out of scope: the plants frontend takes no part in the add-address round trip or the add page reached from the journey.
requirements.why: Plants is not wired to the INS address book and has no handshake today, and a row with no plants equivalent leaves plants alone (ruling 2026-10-09 pm); increments are not split to look for a plants equivalent. Plants does have the party edit page and the review read-back, so it takes those changes in the same increment (req-680 to req-693).

requirements.statement: On the add-address page reached from a party picker, 'Save and return to address page' makes exactly the same checks as 'Save and select': with any answer missing or not valid the trader stays on the add-address page, sees an error for each one in field order, keeps every value they entered and every role they ticked, and nothing is written to the address book; the address is saved only once every answer passes. A germinal products notification's add-address page behaves the same way.
requirements.why: A second save button must not let a half-checked address into the trader's address book. The owner's 26 October decision is that the save buttons behave consistently, that a missing or invalid answer keeps the trader on the page with an error for each one, and that no page is an exception; the 10 November review restates that both save buttons make the same checks. Germinal products takes live animals as its reference point and reaches the same add page through the same handshake.
requirements.deltaNote: Both save buttons are on the page today (repo-tests-p7-003) and a refused save keeps the page, lists the errors in field order and stores nothing (repo-tests-p7-034, repo-tests-p7-035), but nothing drives that refusal from the second save: the Design Release 2.1 suite lists the errors only from 'Save and select' (prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-066) and submits 'Save and return to address page' only with a complete address (prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-068). The second save button itself is req-673 and the check set it applies is req-660 to req-668.

requirements.statement: The add-address page asks for 'County (optional)' between 'Town or city' and 'Postcode or Zip code', which the trader may leave blank.
requirements.why: The ruling of 14 October 2026 keeps County on the address book's add-details step, which is the step the journey's add-address page is: the V4 Address Block gives every address block the same fields, County included, and an add form that cannot set a field the record, the view page and the edit form all carry would lose that data on a round trip.
requirements.deltaNote: The page already offers 'County (optional)' in that position, as a half-width input the trader may leave blank (repo-tests-p7-015, trace-e2e-p9-062, trace-e2e-p9-062-m1). Its length cap is req-668's 100 characters.

requirements.statement: On the consignee, importer and place of destination party edit pages the Country select holds 'United Kingdom' alone and the saved country is United Kingdom; the place of origin, consignor and consignment contact edit pages offer the whole country list. The plants frontend's place of destination edit page does the same.
requirements.why: The address book refuses a consignee, importer or place of destination outside the United Kingdom and leaves the other roles unrestricted, so a copy edit that could set another country would make the notification hold an address the book itself would not accept.
requirements.deltaNote: Today all six live animals edit pages apply the same nine rules with the same full country list and nothing depends on which party is being edited (repo-frontend-p15-150, repo-frontend-p15-103), and plants' edit page accepts any country the address book lists, the United States included (repo-plantsfrontend-p8-107, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-069).

requirements.statement: On the party edit page a country the address book does not list is refused with 'Enter a country' in both the live animals and the high-risk plants frontends.
requirements.why: The two frontends show the same page and both take their labels and refusals from the address book, so one unlisted country must not read two ways.
requirements.deltaNote: Live animals refuses both a blank and an unlisted country with 'Enter a country' (repo-frontend-p15-116, repo-tests-p7-063, trace-e2e-p8-051), while plants refuses a blank one with 'Enter a country' and an unlisted one with 'Enter a valid country' (repo-plantsfrontend-p8-105, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-106).

requirements.statement: The party edit page's county field carries the browser autocomplete hint address-level1, as its other address fields carry theirs.
requirements.why: GOV.UK and WCAG 1.3.5 ask an input holding personal data to identify its purpose, and the county is the only address field on the page without a hint.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the live animals edit form sets organization, address-line1, address-line2, address-level2, postal-code, tel and email but nothing on the county (repo-frontend-p15-105); plants already sets address-level1 (repo-plantsfrontend-p8-075), so only live animals changes.

requirements.statement: Out of scope: an exporter role on an address, and an 'Exporter' option among the add-address page's role checkboxes.
requirements.why: The ruling of 16 November 2026 is that no row in any theme adds an EXPORTER role: the address book's whole role vocabulary is the six roles, the prototype's consignor-or-exporter identifier is its own internal type vocabulary read from app/routes.js and app/data, which a row may not rest on whatever a claim from those files is labelled, and what the design means is one section covering both parties under the heading Consignor, which the service already models as the single CONSIGNOR role.

requirements.statement: The add-address hand-off between the animals frontend and the INS address book works in CDP, in the local Docker stack and in the CI Docker stack the pull request end-to-end runs use, each service taking the other's address from its own configuration and never from a hard-coded host or port.
requirements.why: Every link, redirect and form hand-over between services has to work in all three places from each service's own config (ruling 2026-11-04 point 4), and this hand-off is a redirect out of one service and back again.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the hand-off is exercised where both frontends run, the compose stack and CDP, and skipped when the animals frontend runs in stub mode (repo-tests-p7-001, repo-frontend-p15-036, trace-e2e-p9-079); nothing names the CI Docker stack the pull request runs use as a place it is proven, and nothing shows either service reading the other's address from its own configuration.

requirements.statement: Every add-address page reached from the journey, the one reached from the consignment contact page included, ends with the primary button 'Save and select'.
requirements.why: One button doing one thing reads one way, and the contact route's save does select the new address on the page it returns to, just as a party picker's does.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page reached from a party picker reads 'Save and select' (repo-tests-p7-003) while the page reached from the consignment contact page reads 'Save and continue' (repo-tests-p7-016), even though that save also leaves the new branch address chosen on the contact page (repo-tests-p7-018).

requirements.statement: The tests that prove the review page's broken-copy error summary and its inline party errors find the review's cards by GOV.UK structure and role rather than by the words of a numbered heading.
requirements.why: The owner's 19 November decision is that live animals review tests find cards the way the plants tests already do, so renumbering or rewording a card heading does not break a test of the address errors.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the review's broken-copy errors are proven through the error summary and the party's own row (trace-e2e-p8-015, trace-e2e-p8-017), and the ruling records that live animals review tests still reach cards by heading words, which no test may depend on (ruling-sam-2026-11-19-p1-010).

conflicts.about: Where the journey's add-address page lives: inside the animals journey (Design Release 2.1) or on the INS frontend's address book reached by today's handshake.

positions.says: Each role has its own add-address page inside the journey at <section path>/add-address, which saves into the address book.
The prototype holds saved addresses in its own session and calls no address book or notification API, so it cannot show cross-service behaviour.
The prototype wins by default over what the real services do today.
A real constraint the prototype cannot express, such as cross-service behaviour, overrides the prototype.
DR1 left the destination for a person to choose: an add page in the animals frontend, or a link to the INS front door's add page with a way back.
The animals frontend's address-book service reads and never writes by design; the INS frontend is the address book's only writer.
Rhys blocked parity changes on the address pages on 2026-09-04 while the team's address work was live.
'Add a new address' sends the trader to the INS address book's add page with the journey type, notification id, fulfilment id and a one-off handshake token.
The animals journey no longer serves its own create-address page; the old route answers 404.
Outside Design Release 2.1, a section's add-address page redirects to the address book's add page with the section named in from.
The INS address book returns the trader to the journey's address-return endpoint with the fulfilment id, handshake token and the new record's id.
The prototype never decides architecture: the split into sets, journeys and services, URL paths or code structure.
c-106 is not architecture and is unchanged by the ruling.
INS-side germinal work, including the address-book return entry, stays in the INS themes and is proven in the ins Playwright project.
inc-053, the route to add an address from an address-selection page, is blocked by Rhys (2026-09-04) while the team's address work was live.
inc-054, correcting a wrong saved address from a picker, is blocked by Rhys (2026-09-04) for the same reason.
The missing add-address route is an accepted temporary gap: traders go to the address book by themselves.
inc-053 is frontend work because the address-book API already serves create; only where the add page lives is in dispute.

conflicts.outcome: Keep today's handshake and the INS frontend as the address book's only writer, because where the add page is served and which service writes the address book is cross-service behaviour the prototype cannot express (ruling 2026-10-07 claim 10), and ruling 2026-10-09 leaves this conflict unchanged (claim 126) and confirms the prototype never decides which service serves a page (claim 66). The page itself follows Design Release 2.1, and the tests repo now proves most of that page as built: 'Add a new address' crosses to the INS address book's add page, which in journey mode shows the caption, heading, status block, section headings, fields, roles question and the three controls, and returns through the journey's address-return route to the page each control names ('Save and select' commits the copy and lands on the Consignment addresses page, 'Save and return to address page' lands on the picker unselected, 'Cancel and return to hub' saves nothing). It keeps County (optional), which the 14 October ruling holds on this very step (c-party-address-add-and-edit-001), and it stores roles only, with no address type (c-party-address-add-and-edit-003). The picker it returns to shows eight addresses a page and restates the chosen address above the results (ruling:ian-2026-11-25). In journey mode the 'Choose an address type' step is skipped (req-1958); outside a journey the address book's own add follows Design Release 2.1 in full. A germinal products notification uses the same handshake, with its own INS return entry built in the INS themes (ruling 2026-10-09 claim 61). The search parts of the page wait on the address lookup becoming a real feature and are parked as concept work (ruling:sam-2026-11-09); until then every add page opens on manual entry. The hand-off works in CDP, the local Docker stack and the CI Docker stack from each service's own configuration (req-party-address-add-and-edit-006); in the animals frontend's stub mode, where no INS frontend runs, the pickers keep showing no add control. The animals frontend serves no /<role>/add-address page and its address-book service stays read-only. The DR1 blocks on inc-053 and inc-054 (Rhys, 2026-09-04) and DR1's acceptance of the missing add route as a temporary gap are set aside: the team's address work has landed as today's handshake, and the later rulings put this area back in the programme. Each picker row's link to its record (req-1960) goes to the INS address book on the same reasoning; plants takes none of it, because plants is not wired to the INS address book (ruling 2026-10-09 pm).

conflicts.about: The manual-entry Country list: Design Release 2.1's 42 countries, regions and territories against the sovereign states reference-data serves.

positions.says: A parity finding whose fix is the content of a master reference-data list is deferred, not built, because MDM replaces the hard-coded list.
Countries, regions and territories are master reference data the service takes from MDM after the DR1 parity build.
Where DR1 already judged the same difference, its judgement is followed.
The Country select offers 42 entries, including the EU outermost regions and the Crown Dependencies.
The add page's Country select offered 32 sovereign states with United Kingdom pulled to the front.
The add page's Country select now lists 'Select a country' first and then every country reference data serves, alphabetically, with United Kingdom in its alphabetical place.
No reference list waits on MDM integration; every list is built now against reference-data as it is, and its content is what MDM serves.
Where a list's content differs from Design Release 2.1, that is MDM's content to change, never a reason to block a row or to edit a list in code.
The block is taken off the requirements behind c-107, which rested on DR1's MDM judgement.
The INS Country select is reference-data's unfiltered /countries list.

conflicts.outcome: The later ruling (2026-10-09) ranks first and withdraws the MDM block this conflict once applied: req-644 is built against reference-data as it is, and the tests repo now shows the select serving exactly that list (repo-tests-p7-037), so the requirement is met. Design Release 2.1's 42-entry list is not built, because a list whose content differs from the design is MDM's to change, never edited in code. DR1's MDM judgement still stands for who owns list content (ruling 2026-10-09 claim 134), so document-dr1-parity-notes-p1-037 is not overruled; only its deferral rule (p1-038) is. The 'Select one' placeholder is not list content and is still to be built (req-643).

conflicts.about: Whether the add-address page checks only that required fields are filled (Design Release 2.1) or also keeps the address book's length and email-format checks (today).

positions.says: A real constraint the prototype cannot express, naming validation, overrides the prototype.
The address rules check email format, with 'Enter an email address in the correct format'.
The address rules cap postcode at 12 characters, with 'Postcode must be 12 characters or fewer'.
The add-address page only checks each required field is filled, with no format check on postcode, email or phone.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first and names validation as a real constraint the prototype cannot express: the address book stores and checks these limits, so the add page keeps today's length and email-format checks and messages alongside Design Release 2.1's required-field messages. The prototype's required-only rule is set aside.

conflicts.about: Whether the add-address page follows the GOV.UK accessibility patterns the prototype leaves out: the 'Error: ' title prefix and 400 status on a refused submit, autocomplete hints on personal-data fields, and error summary links that reach a visible field.

positions.says: A real constraint the prototype cannot express, such as validation, overrides the prototype.
Today's address forms prefix the title with 'Error: ' when a submit is refused.
The journey's party edit form's fields carry autocomplete hints: organization, address-line1, address-line2, address-level2, postal-code, tel and email.
On the add page every field but the name carries its autocomplete hint; the name field carries none.
The prototype's refused submit keeps the plain title with no 'Error: ' prefix and answers 200.
No add-address input carries an autocomplete attribute.
On the search pages the error summary links point at fields that are hidden.
Every field on the plants party edit page carries its autofill hint, address-level1 for the county included.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: how validation errors are reported, and what assistive technology needs from a form, are real constraints (GOV.UK error pattern, WCAG 2.2 AA under the public sector accessibility regulations) that a session-only prototype is not held to and does not express. The add page keeps the 'Error: ' prefix, the 400 status and autocomplete hints, and reveals the fields on the search pages so summary links reach them. Most of the hints are now set, leaving the name field on the add page (req-670) and the county field on the party edit page (req-party-address-add-and-edit-004), which plants already sets. The prototype's plain error title and missing autocomplete are set aside. trace-prototype-dr2-1-p7-051 is not overruled: its six messages and their order still stand; only its hidden-field links are departed from.

conflicts.about: Address search's JavaScript-only behaviour in Design Release 2.1 (results as the trader types, the search-only layout that hides the fields, 'Enter address manually', custom announcements) against the 9 October afternoon ruling's graceful-degradation and toolbox rules.

positions.says: Results list as the trader types, with the typed text in bold.
The address fields and uses checkboxes stay hidden until a result is picked or manual entry is chosen.
Results appear in the browser as the trader types.
Every page works fully without JavaScript, and JavaScript may only enhance a page that already works.
The prototype's search mechanics are not copied; anything beyond the component's own options, such as custom announcements, waits on design.
Filtering as the trader types waits on design question 5; search on the Search button or Enter is built.
The fields hidden behind the search, 'Enter address manually' and the search-only layout that reveals the fields wait as one waiting-on-design increment (design question 10).
The rest of address search stays blocked on the address lookup, and the design increment is blocked on it too.
Design is asked whether address search can use the GOV.UK address pattern with the fields always visible.
Address searching is built without live filtering: the search does not filter as the trader types, and the trader types a term then presses Search or Enter.
This ruling does not settle address search's search-only layout or its lookup results as you type, which stay deferred as concept work under ruling:sam-2026-11-09 point 2.
Address search is concept work and is not needed for the deadline, so it is not built yet, while the requirements behind it stay adopted and parked.
The add-address pages show every field from the start, as the real service's main branch has them, rather than offering an address search first.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October afternoon ruling ranks first, and the two later rulings narrow it rather than reverse it. When the address lookup lands, the version that works without JavaScript is built: a search form submitted by its 'Search' button or Enter (req-647), results on the returned page (req-648), and a pick that fills the fields (req-650). Design's 13 November decision confirms there is no live filtering of the picker's own address rows, and its own point 7 keeps the lookup's results-as-you-type with the deferred concept work rather than deciding it, so req-1957 stays adopted and blocked rather than dropped. The JavaScript-only parts stay adopted but blocked on design as well as the lookup, in the waiting-on-design theme: results as the trader types with bold matches (req-1957), the custom result-count announcement (req-649), and the search-only layout with 'Enter address manually' and its errors (req-652, req-653, req-654). Ruling:sam-2026-11-09 parks the whole of address search as concept work, so every one of those requirements carries that parking as well. Until then every add-address page opens on manual entry with the fields shown (req-1830), which is what the owner's 9 November decision keeps. Nothing is overruled: design may still keep or drop each behaviour.

conflicts.about: Whether the add-address page reached from the journey asks for County: Design Release 2.1's manual-entry fields leave it out, and the 14 October 2026 ruling keeps it on the address book's add-details step, which is the same step.

positions.says: Manual address entry on the add-address page has the fields name, address line 1, address line 2, town or city, postcode and country, with no County.
The suite asserts the add page's field set without a County field.
The prototype nonetheless stores the chosen address on the section as 'town, county, postcode' joined by commas, so its own copy carries a county the form cannot set.
The address book's add-details step keeps its County field; it is not removed.
V4's Address Block gives every address block the same fields, County included, and ranks above the prototype, so a Design Release 2.1 page leaving County out is a prototype mistake.
An add form that cannot set a field the record, the view page and the edit form all carry would lose that data on a round trip.
The ruling decides only the address book's add-details step and does not say whether County must be added on any other page where Design Release 2.1 omits it.
The prototype still decides how a page looks and reads, including which fields a page shows and in what order.
Where a piece of data is a field the notification captures, V4 specifies it, and no row rests on the prototype for what data is captured.
The add page's nine fields today include 'County (optional)' between 'Town or city' and 'Postcode or Zip code'.
The add page offers 'County (optional)', which the user may leave blank.

conflicts.outcome: The 14 October 2026 ruling wins and 'County (optional)' stays, so req-642 comes out of scope and req-party-address-add-and-edit-001 takes its place. The ruling decides the address book's add-details step by name, and the page the journey reaches is that step in journey mode (req-1958), not another page, so the open point its claim 17 records about other pages does not reach it. Its ground holds with full force here: the page writes the same address-book record the view and edit pages show County on, so an add form without County would lose the field on a round trip, which is a real persistence constraint the prototype cannot express under ruling:sam-2026-10-07 claim 10. Ruling:ian-2026-11-11 ranks higher but pulls both ways and names no field: its claim 15 gives the prototype which fields a page shows, while its claim 13 gives V4 the fields a record captures, and its own closing claim says the ruling changes nothing else in the backlog, so it does not withdraw a ruling that decided this very step. prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-083 and prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-060 are not overruled, because their section heading, labels and field order still stand and are built on by req-638, req-640, req-641 and req-645; only the absence of County in their field list is departed from. County's cap stays the address book's 100 characters (req-668).

conflicts.about: Whether the add page the journey reaches is already Design Release 2.1's 'Add address and contact details' page, as the tests repo asserts, or still the earlier 'Add address details' page the end-to-end traces show.

positions.says: The page reached from the journey is headed 'Add address and contact details' with the caption 'Add new address' and the matching browser title.

It groups its fields under 'Address' and 'Contact details', shows the notification's Draft tag and reference, offers a Back link, 'Save and select', 'Save and return to address page' and 'Cancel and return to hub', and asks the roles question.
Reached from the consignee picker it asks the roles question legended 'What else should this address be used for?' with the design's own hint.
The page reached from the journey is headed 'Add address details', with no caption and no back link.
It groups its fields under 'Enter address details' and 'Enter contact details'.
It ends with a primary 'Save and continue' and a secondary 'Cancel and return to address page', and asks no roles question.

conflicts.outcome: The tests repo ranks above the end-to-end traces and describes the page as it now stands: the traces were captured against an earlier build of the same specs, which is why they still show 'Add address details'. So req-634 to req-641, req-645, req-655 to req-659, req-661 to req-663, req-665 to req-667 and req-671 to req-676 are already met, and what is left on the page is the 'Select one' placeholder (req-643), the United Kingdom-only select for destination-side roles (req-646), the name error wording (req-660), the country error wording (req-664), the name field's autocomplete hint (req-670), the type-step skip (req-1958), the second save's checks (req-2186) and the contact route's button wording (c-party-address-add-and-edit-005). Nothing is overruled: each trace claim truthfully records the page at the moment it was captured, and each is still the evidence of what the page used to show, which is what the deltaNotes name.

conflicts.about: What a journey-added address record holds: the prototype's section as the address's type, or roles only with the type derived by the INS front door.

positions.says: A new consignment address would be stored with a consignment-added id and the section as its type, carrying email and telephone.
The address book stores roles only, requires at least one, does not store an address type and ignores one a client sends.
The address type is the INS front door's grouping of roles, worked out from the roles an address holds.
An address's type is derivable from its roles, which is why ruling:paul-2026-11-05 dropped it, unlike a transporter's intrinsic private-or-commercial type.
An address saved by Save and select holds exactly the role of the picker it was reached from, and both CONSIGNEE and IMPORTER when Importer is ticked.

conflicts.outcome: The 5 November 2026 ruling ranks first and settles the record: roles only, at least one, no stored address type, with a type a client sends ignored and the front door deriving the type from the roles instead. The prototype's section-as-type is set aside as its own session storage, which under ruling:sam-2026-10-09 claim 116 is the address book service's design rather than look and feel. req-659 is reworded to roles only and no longer rests on the prototype's storage claim.

conflicts.about: Which CDP environment the add-address hand-off between the animals frontend and the INS address book has to work in, and what proves it works in all three places the ruling names.

positions.says: Links, redirects and form hand-overs between services must work in CDP, in the local Docker stack and in the CI Docker stack the pull request end-to-end runs use, each taking its address from the service's own configuration.
The ruling names CDP as a whole and no environment within it, such as dev, test or production.
The ruling does not say how working links in all three places are to be proved, so no check or evidence is named.
The hand-off is only exercised where both frontends run, the compose stack and CDP, and is skipped when the animals frontend runs in stub mode.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling plainly covers the hand-off, so req-party-address-add-and-edit-006 is adopted for the three places it names; what it leaves open is which CDP environment and what counts as proof, and the ruling itself records both as unstated. Taking one plain reading would either over-build a CDP-only check nobody asked for or let CDP go unproven.
conflicts.question: Which CDP environments must the add-address hand-off be proved in, and what counts as proof there, given the hand-off cannot run in the animals frontend's stub mode at all?
conflicts.default: Each environment gets what it can carry: the local Docker stack and the CI Docker stack the pull request runs use are proved by the tests repo's existing hand-off specs, which run only where both frontends are up; CDP dev and test, where both frontends and the address book are deployed, are proved by the same specs in the scheduled CDP run; CDP environments without both frontends and the animals frontend's stub mode are out, and the pickers there show no add control.

conflicts.about: Whether the add-address page reached from the consignment contact page reads 'Save and select' like the five party pages, or keeps today's 'Save and continue'.

positions.says: Outside the address book journey, the add-address page's buttons are 'Save and select' and a secondary 'Save and return to address page', with a 'Cancel and return to hub' link.
The page reached from a party picker offers Back, 'Save and select', 'Save and return to address page' and 'Cancel and return to hub'.
'Save and continue' on the page reached from the contact address page returns to the contact address page with the added banner.
The newly added branch address is the option shown as chosen on the contact address page, so the contact route's save does select it.

conflicts.outcome: The design names the add page's buttons once and never distinguishes the contact route, and the real service reads one way from a party picker and another from the contact page, so the same button on the same page carries two labels with nothing to rank them. Precedence cannot settle it, because both labels come from the same today source describing two routes into one page.
conflicts.question: Does the add-address page reached from the consignment contact page read 'Save and select' like the five party pages, or keep 'Save and continue'?
conflicts.default: 'Save and select' on every add-address page reached from the journey, the contact route included, because that save also leaves the new branch address chosen on the page it returns to, so one button on one page reads one way.
